Modern.brandNameRationale: The colophon is the printer's signature mark at the end of a book — a tradition since the Aldine Press in 1499. Naming a modern printing studio after the printer's mark itself signals respect for the trade. & Co. closes it as a small modern shop.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern printing has split between digital-only DTC operators and a small considered-letterpress cohort of independent shops. The opening is for a studio that puts the printer's mark itself in the brand position and builds a small permanent catalog of letterpress stationery, posters, and book work.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Hatch Show Print (hatchshowprint.com) holds the heritage-letterpress slot. Studio On Fire (studioonfire.com) sits in the design-led letterpress tier. The Aviary Press (aviarypress.com) plays the considered-modern peer. We sit closer to Studio On Fire with a sharper colophon-led framing.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern letterpress studio organized around the printer's mark.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Buys wedding stationery and limited-edition prints. Knows the difference between Vandercook and Heidelberg.
behaviors: Buys posters for the impression, not the image

dos: Show the impression in raking light
Name the press and the paper

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Colophon & Co. set in a clean modern grotesk, with a small printer's-mark cartouche beside the word. The cartouche alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for paper specs and dimensions
typography.rationale: One family. Mono carries the technical printing data.

Luxury.tagline: Fine printing in the Morris tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Kelmscott Press was William Morris's private press at Kelmscott Manor (1891–98) — the foundational Arts & Crafts fine-press operation. Caslon is the foundational English typeface (William Caslon, 1722). Paired with an ampersand, the press lineage and the type lineage ground the brand in 250 years of English fine printing. Both are public-domain historical references.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury fine printing at the private-press tier serves the buyer who commissions a single edition — a poem, a memoir, a wedding book — printed by hand on dampened cotton. The product is a small permanent catalog of editions, finished by hand, signed by the printer.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Arion Press (arionpress.com) is the institutional American fine-press benchmark. Foolscap Press (foolscappress.com) holds the considered-American slot. Whittington Press (whittingtonpress.com) is the considered-English peer. We sit between Arion and Whittington with a sharper Kelmscott-and-Caslon framing.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A fine letterpress in the Kelmscott tradition, set in Caslon, printed by hand.

targetAudience.primary: 55 to 80. Collects fine-press editions. Owns at least one Arion Press book. Commissions one edition every two years.
behaviors: Travels to the press for the proofing visit
Pays in three installments over twelve months

dos: Show the impression in raking light
Name the paper and the binder

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Kelmscott & Caslon set in Caslon roman with a small embossed printer's-mark cartouche in the Kelmscott tradition. The cartouche appears on the colophon page of every edition.

typography.primary: Adobe Caslon for the wordmark and the editions
typography.secondary: Adobe Caslon for body and commission documents
typography.rationale: Caslon throughout. The brand is the type lineage.

Minimal.tagline: The wedge that holds the form.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: A quoin is the metal wedge that locks the type form in the chase before it goes on the press — single trade word, single syllable, deeply specific. Single-word naming follows the apothecary-minimal school applied to printing.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal printing brands have converged on monoline-sans aesthetics. The opening underneath is a letterpress stripped to the tool that holds the type in place — the quoin — with a small permanent catalog of plain printed work.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Studio On Fire (studioonfire.com) holds the considered-modern letterpress slot. Smock Paper (smockpaper.com) sits in the considered-bamboo peer position. Egg Press (eggpress.com) plays the considered-letterpress peer. We sit closer to Smock with a sharper single-tool focus.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Plain letterpress, stripped to the type form.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Buys plain printed stationery and posters. Will wait six weeks for the right impression.
behaviors: Buys one print every six months

dos: Name the paper and the press
donts: Use the word minimal as marketing

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only — Quoin set in a calm humanist sans, lowercase. A small quoin-wedge mark serves as the favicon.

typography.primary: Neue Haas Grotesk for the wordmark and body
typography.rationale: One face. The brand is the quoin, not the type.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Stanley Morison was the typographic adviser to Monotype Corporation (designed Times New Roman, 1932) and the foundational English commercial typographer. Pike is an invented partner surname pulled from the English printing trade. Paired with Printers, the name reads as an established commercial print firm.
Corporate.industrySummary: Commercial printing is a serious B2B category. The buyers are publishers, corporate marketing teams, and packaging procurement managers. The vendors compete on color accuracy, lead time, and on-time delivery across millions of impressions.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: RR Donnelley (rrd.com) is the institutional commercial-printing benchmark. Quad (quad.com) holds the marketing-services peer slot. Sheridan (sheridan.com) is the publisher-printing peer. We sit smaller, sharper on the typographic-quality specification.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Commercial printing for publishers and marketing teams — color-accurate, on schedule, typographically literate.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 60. Production directors at publishers and marketing operations VPs at corporate teams.

dos: Quote lead times to the day

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark — a stylized chase-and-quoin silhouette. MORISON & PIKE PRINTERS set in Times New Roman, suitable for B2B spec sheets and trade-show banners.

typography.primary: Times New Roman for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Inter for body and B2B materials
typography.rationale: Times for the typographic lineage. Inter for digital legibility.

Creative.brandNameRationale: The printer's devil is the apprentice in the print shop — the boy who fetched type, cleaned the press, and ended up covered in ink. The plural pluralizes the apprenticeship. The brand sits on the lifelong-apprentice posture of the trade.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative printing has been crowded with overly precious letterpress aesthetics. The opening is for a print shop with a working sense of humor — posters, zines, broadsides, postcards — printed on whatever press is open that week.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Hatch Show Print (hatchshowprint.com) holds the heritage poster-letterpress slot. Yee-Haw Industries (yeehawindustries.com) sits in the considered-creative peer position. Globe Poster (globeposters.com) plays the heritage broadside peer. We sit closer to Yee-Haw with a sharper apprentice's voice.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative letterpress shop in the apprentice-and-poster tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Buys posters and zines. Reads about printing history. Will pay for the impression and the joke.
behaviors: Re-orders the same paper for the next run

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — Ink Devils set in a punchy slab serif with a small drawn mark of two ink-stained hands holding a composing stick. The hands alone are the favicon.

typography.primary: Knockout for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT Sectra for body and broadside copy
typography.rationale: Knockout carries the broadside voice. Sectra handles the longer-form essays.
